_comment: Thresholds for tools/loop. 'hard' gates fail the run: they mean the output is broken. 'target' gates only warn: they describe where the redesign is heading and are expected to fail until that work lands. All values are provisional until calibrated against human ratings (see docs/loop/README.md).

active_area.why: most of the frame should be filled, not objects on black

jerkiness.why: motion should not flicker (review 1: a clip held under 0.6 was rated too smooth, so smoothness is no longer a target in itself)

audio_sync.why: the picture should visibly follow the music

variety.why: the look should evolve over the clip

punch.why: the picture should jump on the music's hits, not ease through them (review 1: about 1.1 was rated 'not punchy')

look_change.why: the picture should not look the same as eight seconds ago (review 1: 0.10 to 0.16 was 'boring after less than 10 s')

one_hue_share.why: not one colour everywhere (review 1: 0.69 to 0.76, nearly all magenta, was rated ugly)

wash.why: not a fog of saturated mid-tone colour (review 1: 0.21 to 0.33 was rated ugly)

accuracy._comment: Thresholds for tools/loop/accuracy.py. Instrument checks and regressions against accuracy_baseline.json are hard failures and need no entry here. These are targets: they warn, and describe where the analysis should get to.

onset_bias_ms.why: mean timing error under one 60 fps frame

onset_f.why: most audible events found, few false alarms

percussive_recall.why: fast attacks are the events visuals lock to

soft_recall.why: slow attacks (pads, swells) should not be ignored

beat_f.why: beat grid on the beat at some metrical level

tempo_right.why: tempo correct at some metrical level (half, double, a third or triple also count)

stem_improvement_db.why: separation clearly better than handing back the mix

regression.why: best held-out score may not fall against the saved baseline
